summary: Irving Babbitt worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Harvard College, Williams College, the University of Paris, and Harvard University. He held positions at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).

Isaac Schapera worked in history and archaeology and other fields. He studied at the University of Cape Town, Cándido Candi, and the London School of Economics. His posts included the University of Chicago (~1948–1949), LSE (~1950–1969), and the University of Toronto.

Isaak Jakob Schmidt was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctoral degree from the University of Rostock. He served at the Russian Bible Society and became a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1838–1847).

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy works in Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Harvard University, Tibet University, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts at Laval University in ~2004 and 2007.

Isabelle Onians is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 2002 and served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library (attested 2007).

Isabelle Ratié works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig (~2009–2013), Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

Isaiah Berlin was a philosopher and historian. He was educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1928–1932), and held an academic appointment at the University of Oxford from ~1932 to 1975.

Isaline Blew Horner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held posts at Newnham College (1918, 1923), Cambridge (1939–1949), and the Pali Text Society (1942, 1959–1981).
Isamu Kanaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Shitennoji University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Isao Nishitani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, later serving at Fort William College (1841–1846, 1849), Sanskrit College (1846–1849), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1851).

Iso Kern is a philosopher and scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at KU Leuven, Freiburg, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University, he held posts at KU Leuven (1962–1971), Heidelberg (~1973–1979), Bern (1985), Zurich, and Fribourg.
Issaien Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and subsequently held a post as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Sophia University and completed a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology. She studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and was attested as a teaching professor at the University of Washington in 2026.

Ivan Minayev was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1858–1862) and held a post at the university's Faculty of Oriental Studies from ~1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber, later serving as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard was a linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held positions at Harvard University (~1969–1975), the National Museum of Natural History (~1975), and the Smithsonian Institution (~1975).
